pos.personaBrief: Short flat passing and a famous combination play (de.wikipedia, WSC 1932) show a side that wanted the ball and controlled play through it, with no sign of a counter-attacking identity.

pro.personaBrief: Short flat ground passes, the web of inter-passing and Sindelar's ground pass (WSC 1932) point to patient build-up, not quick vertical play.

est.personaBrief: The Whirl meant perpetual interchange among all ten outfield players, with a withdrawn centre-forward and close combination (gottfriedfuchs, Irish Times), so it was relational.

lar.personaBrief: A classic 2-3-5 kept real wingers (Zischek, Vogl, who ran and crossed), but the game was built on central combination around Sindelar and Smistik.

blo.personaBrief: No pressing evidence; the retreating defence of 1932 and a team built around combination suggest a non-pressing side that waited, though not an ultra-deep block (Hiden came far off his line).

mar.personaBrief: Weak evidence: Sesta was renowned for man-marking and robust play, and the era's British-style 2-3-5 matched backs to opposing forwards, so the lean is slightly towards man-marking.

pla.personaBrief: Meisl's answer at 0-2 was 'Spüts euer Spüü' (play your game), and the team kept the 2-3-5 and short-passing identity against everyone.

res.personaBrief: The Wunderteam is remembered for style and the praise of British press rather than trophies, and played its own game even when losing, so it leans towards spectacle.

sis.personaBrief: A collective, fluid whirl in which no one was purely attacker or defender, with little individual dribbling, yet Sindelar had a free role; the system leaned ahead of the individual.

jog.personaBrief: Sindelar 'no brawn but any amount of brain', British praise for ball control and technique: a technical side.

bas.personaBrief: Meisl rebuilt the team in 1931 with debutants but kept a stable core of Vienna players through 1931-32; neither a youth nor a veteran emphasis is clear, with an experienced stable core slightly ahead.

lid.personaBrief: Meisl bowed to public pressure on Sindelar and told players to play their game, but he was also a dominant organiser who could rage after defeats; moderately authoritarian with pragmatic flexibility.
